proposal.description_long: In June 2019, Manhattan prosecutors were preparing to prosecute Paul Manafort on New York state charges while he was serving a federal sentence. NBC News, citing contemporaneous reporting and officials, said Manafort’s lawyer asked the Bureau of Prisons to keep him in federal custody because of concerns about his health and safety at Rikers Island. Deputy Attorney General Jeffrey Rosen then contacted Manhattan District Attorney Cyrus Vance’s office, attached the lawyer’s letter, and asked for its response. Vance’s office said it had not proposed housing Manafort at Rikers and took no position on whether he should remain in federal custody. Federal officials ultimately kept Manafort in federal custody at the Metropolitan Correctional Center while making him available to state prosecutors. The available accounts support DOJ involvement in the placement decision after a defense request, but not the original claim that DOJ independently ordered Manafort kept out of Rikers. The record also does not establish political direction from Trump.
